thesis: Mohnish Pabrai argues that humans are fixed after age six and that life is too short to seek revenge on enemies, suggesting one should instead ignore them and minimize time spent with them. He explains that he chose investing after hearing about Warren Buffett at age 30, realizing the power of compounding which allowed Buffett to grow $10,000 into approximately $250 billion through a 26% annual return rate starting at age 18. Pabrai states that he applied this approach to his own $1 million from selling a portion of his IT company in 1994, achieving a 70% annual increase until 2000 and a 36% annual increase until 2007 before rates declined to 10-12%.
